title: Equivariance transport in prop:lefschetz: tau_* = conjugation-by-t on rational K(Gamma_0,1) not fully justified

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location.** `prop:lefschetz` (necessary fixed-point condition) and `lem:qhomology`.

**The gap (likely closable, but currently terse).** The proof identifies the Lefschetz number of the deck involution $\tau$ on $M_0$ with that of the isometry $\sigma$ on $N_0=\Gamma_0\backslash X$, via the claim that the $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbb{Z}/2]$-module structure on rational homology "is intrinsic to the pair $(\Gamma_0,t)$, hence the same on the rational homology of any $K(\Gamma_0,1)$."

For $N_0$ (genuinely aspherical) the action on $H_*(N_0;\mathbb{Q})=H_*(\Gamma_0;\mathbb{Q})$ is conjugation-by-$t$ and is canonical. But $M_0$ is only a **rational** $K(\Gamma_0,1)$; to conclude $\tau_*$ corresponds to conjugation-by-$t$ one must know the isomorphism of `lem:qhomology` (induced by the classifying map $M_0\to B\Gamma_0$) **intertwines** $\tau_*$ with the conjugation action. `lem:qhomology` asserts naturality/$Q$-equivariance, but the displayed justification ("the deck action of $q$ covers a self-homotopy-equivalence inducing conjugation by a lift of $q$") is terse and is exactly the place where rational-vs-equivariant transport must be pinned down (cf. resolved q7-8, re-introduced in a new form).

**Fix.** State explicitly that the classifying map $M_0\to B\Gamma_0$ is, up to homotopy, $\tau$-equivariant for the deck involution covering $\bar t$ (it induces on $\pi_1$ the conjugation by a lift of $\bar t$, and maps into the aspherical $B\Gamma_0$ are determined up to homotopy by their $\pi_1$-effect), so the `lem:qhomology` iso intertwines $\tau_*$ and conjugation-by-$t$, giving $L(\tau)=L(\sigma)$.

This does not appear to be fatal, but the necessary-condition argument is incomplete without it.
